steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: This topic covers key vocabulary and structures for going out and entertainment. You need to know the topic vocabulary, be able to use it in all four skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing), and express opinions with reasons.

steps.title: French Exam Tips — Going Out and Entertainment
steps.body: 1. For Going Out and Entertainment, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Going Out and Entertainment, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Write 4 sentences in French about going out and entertainment. | Write a paragraph (40-60 words) giving your opinion on going out and entertainment. | Translate into French: "I think going out and entertainment is important because..."

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Four sentences using topic vocabulary, with correct adjective agreement, articles and verb conjugation. Include at least two different tenses for Higher tier. | A structured paragraph with: introduction (à mon avis...), opinion with reason (je pense que... parce que...), a different viewpoint (cependant...), and a conclusion (en conclusion...). Use connecting | "Je pense que [topic] est important(e) parce que..." — ensure adjective agreement (important vs importante depending on noun gender), correct verb form, and give a specific reason.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use a range of tenses (present, past, future) to access higher marks Include opinions with reasons (je pense que... parce que...) Check adjective agreement (gender and number) before finishing Use complex structures: negation (ne...pas, ne...jamais), pronouns (le, la, les), conjunctions (cependant, donc, en plus) Include cultural references to French-speaking countries For writing: plan your response, check verb conjugations, re-read for errors
